newsitem.title: THAILAND: Baht fails to shake off devaluation rumour.
newsitem.headline: Baht fails to shake off devaluation rumour.

text.p: The battered Thai baht failed on Friday to shake off persistent devaluation rumours fuelled by disappointment in economic indicators and talk that a major finance company faced financial problems.

"The baht devaluation talk could be traced to jitters about the overall economic and financial sector outlook which, some fear, may deteriorate to a situation seen in Japan," said Chatchawan Jumruswittayawong, a currency dealer at Bank of Ayudhya Plc.
The central Bank of Thailand has denied the devaluation rumours.

Some analysts said talk earlier this week that Finance One Plc faced problems in meeting its debt service obligations also added to market jitters about the overall health of the financial sector. Finance One, Thailand's biggest finance firm, has denied the rumour.

The renewed selling of the baht, which has hovered at a 6-1/2 year low this week, caused stocks to tumble although the currency managed to hold just above the psychological low of 26 baht to the U.S. dollar seen on Thursday.

The baht traded at 25.939/25.944 to the dollar late on Friday. Dealers said heavy speculative dollar selling in favour of the baht by a major foreign fund manager might have prevented the Thai currency from breaching the 26-baht mark.

The Thai bourse's composite SET Index tumbled 3.92 percent late on Friday to 788.04 points. Brokers said the weak baht triggered the stock selloff which pushed bank and finance counters down 4.92 percent and 4.65 percent, respectively.
Currency dealers said they did not see evidence of central bank intervention to prop up the baht on Friday. The central bank was forced to step in twice to support the currency on Thursday.
Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday he could not see any reason for devaluing a weaker baht which, he said, should help exports.
A senior central bank official on Thursday warned speculators that the authorities would take necessary measures to stabilise the currency.

The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday the Thai balance of payments posted a rare deficit of 19.2 billion baht in December, its second deficit in two months. But it discounted the deficit as seasonal, saying it should swing into a surplus in January.
The bank said the government also posted a hefty budget deficit for the October-December quarter.

Thanasak Chantarovas, deputy director of the central bank's banking department, said on Friday market concerns about Thailand's financial position and scepticism about a government plan to curb expenditure helped sustain the devaluation rumour.

Chatchawan of Bank of Ayudhya said market perceptions that the country's financial position was deteriorating and the Finance One rumour outweighed positive news on smaller November trade and current account deficit figures released by the central bank.
"Speculators seize on these issues to spread the baht devaluation rumour to make money. The talk hurt the stock market," another dealer at a foreign bank said.
